# Baghdad 830 – Economy & finance

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/islamic-830-baghdad.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Coinage (stamped metal money)** [`coinage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coinage.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Gold dinar (about 4.25 g), silver dirham (about 2.9 g), copper fulus for small change, all purely inscribed. Al-Ma'mun's reform type of the 820s adds a Quran verse in the outer margin. Big sums are weighed; money changers profit on the rate. Local: mint of Madinat al-Salam; money changers (sarrafun) of Karkh.
- **Double-entry bookkeeping** [`double_entry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/double_entry.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Bureaus keep day books and monthly and annual summaries in words, with their own clerks' notation. Two-sided accounts that must balance are not used; merchants keep simple lists of debts. Local: diwan al-zimam.
- **Interest-bearing loans, pledges and limits on debt bondage** [`interest_loans_collateral`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/interest_loans_collateral.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Interest (riba) is forbidden, so credit runs through deferred-price sales, advance purchase (salam), pledges and double-sale tricks. A qadi may jail a debtor who can pay and will not.
- **Deposit banking and bills of exchange** [`banking_credit`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/banking_credit.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Written payment orders (sakk) are old; the suftaja, a loan repaid in another city, is spreading among merchants and officials. Court bankers (jahbadh) handling state funds are better attested a few decades later. Local: money changers of Karkh; Basra merchants. Elsewhere: Tang China, 'flying money' remittance certificates.
- **Paper money** [`paper_money`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/paper_money.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Paper, seals and trusted bureaus exist, so notes could be made. Accepting a slip of paper for silver would need the state to take it back in taxes, and jurists would fear gharar. Elsewhere: Tang China, flying money (not yet currency).
- **Money supply, debasement and inflation** [`quantity_theory_inflation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quantity_theory_inflation.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Abbasid silver is good, so debasement is not the issue. Prices are blamed on hoarders, bad harvests and war, like the famine of the siege of 812–813. Nobody connects prices with the coin the caliph spends.
- **Risk-sharing partnership (commenda, mudaraba)** [`partnership_commenda`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/partnership_commenda.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Mudaraba (qirad) is standard, worked out by the Hanafis (al-Shaybani); the investor bears the loss, the agent his labour. Partnerships carry Basra's trade to India and China. Local: Basra and Siraf merchants.
- **Joint-stock company and limited liability** [`joint_stock_company`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/joint_stock_company.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. The law knows partners, not a legal person that outlives them. A partnership dissolves at a death, and shares cannot be sold to strangers.
- **Insurance (marine, fire, life)** [`insurance`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/insurance.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. The aqila kin group shares blood money; seafarers share jettisoned cargo by custom. A paid premium against a chance loss looks to jurists like gambling (gharar, maysir).
- **Life tables and the pricing of annuities** [`life_tables_annuities`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/life_tables_annuities.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Inheritance arithmetic fills half of al-Khwarizmi's al-Jabr, but no one records ages at death, and annuities would run into the ban on interest. Local: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi.
- **Public debt and government bonds** [`public_debt_bonds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/public_debt_bonds.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. The caliph borrows from rich officials and merchants when pay runs out, and tax farmers advance revenue. Nothing is standard, transferable or interest-bearing.
- **Stock exchange (securities market)** [`stock_exchange`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/stock_exchange.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Central bank and lender of last resort** [`central_bank`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/central_bank.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. There is the public treasury (bayt al-mal) and the caliph's privy purse, and he spends from both.
- **Division of labour and specialisation** [`division_of_labour`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/division_of_labour.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Baghdad's markets are divided street by street by trade, from paper to perfume. Plato's point that a city needs many specialists is known. No one has taken a single trade apart into steps. Local: Karkh markets; paper makers and copyists.
- **Comparative advantage and free trade** [`comparative_advantage_free_trade`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/comparative_advantage_free_trade.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Egyptian linen, Khurasani cotton, Indian pepper and Chinese silk and stoneware meet in Baghdad. Customs dues are levied at frontiers and ports. Nobody theorises why both sides gain.
- **Prices, supply and demand** [`price_mechanism_supply_demand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/price_mechanism_supply_demand.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. A hadith has the Prophet refuse to fix prices ('God is the one who sets them'); hoarding food is condemned. Governors still fix grain prices in a crisis.
- **Public granaries and price stabilisation (ever-normal granary)** [`ever_normal_granary`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ever_normal_granary.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Everyone knows Joseph storing grain for seven lean years (Quran, sura 12). The state keeps stores for the army and court, not a buffer for prices. Elsewhere: Tang China, ever-normal granaries.
- **Income tax and progressive rates** [`progressive_income_tax`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/progressive_income_tax.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. Jizya is graded in three classes by wealth (48, 24 or 12 dirhams a year); zakat takes a fixed share above a threshold; land tax is by area or a share of the crop. Income as such is never assessed. Local: diwan al-kharaj.
- **Savings banks, credit and consumer cooperatives** [`cooperatives_savings_banks`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cooperatives_savings_banks.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. The poor save in jewellery and keep coin with a trusted neighbour or merchant. Interest on deposits would be riba.
- **Wealth as productivity; sustained economic growth** [`economic_growth_productivity`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/economic_growth_productivity.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. The Persian idea that a just ruler's revenue depends on cultivated, prospering land ('imara) is common; Tahir ibn al-Husayn's letter to his son (821) says so. Wealth means land, tax and treasure. Local: Tahir's letter to Abdallah ibn Tahir.
- **National income accounts (GDP)** [`national_accounts_gdp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/national_accounts_gdp.md) — K1, use partial, make hard, accept low. Revenue lists by province, in coin and kind, are a rough map of what the empire produces. Output itself is never counted.
- **Fighting slumps by sustaining demand (Keynesian policy)** [`aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aggregate_demand_countercyclical_policy.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Caliphs build canals and palaces for glory and hand out gifts in bad years, not on any theory.
